messages:
maria: Heads-up — customer reported their TTFT / tokens/sec graphs flipping negative and showing spikes around 03:12 UTC. Screenshot + timeline in the ticket. Looks correlated with yesterday's streaming rollouts. @erin can you triage?

erin: Thanks — can you paste the customer_id and a short query I can run in the console to pull raw rollup rows? e.g. what window range?

maria: customer_id: acme-inc. Problem window 2026-03-15T03:00:00 -> 2026-03-15T03:20:00. Quick query I ran: `SELECT window_start, tokens_sec, token_delta FROM streaming_rollups WHERE customer_id='acme-inc' AND window_start >= '2026-03-15T03:00:00' ORDER BY window_start;` results attached — several `tokens_sec` rows are negative, some large magnitude.

devon: Negative token deltas usually mean a consumer offset moved backwards or a rollup compaction bug. Did we change the rollup window size? I vaguely recall a config tweak last night to make windows smaller for low-latency dashboards.

maria: ops PR `ops/rollup-window-shortening` merged 2100011100 — changed `rollup.window_ms` from 60000 -> 15000 for the streaming pipeline.

jay: We had a consumer rebalance at 2100011205 (kafka consumer group: stream-rollup-v2). Logs show an offset reset for partition 3 -> `offset reset to earliest` because ephemeral checkpoint was missing after deploy. Snippet:  `INFO 2026-03-15T03:20:05Z consumer.Rebalance - resetting offsets to earliest for group=stream-rollup-v2, partition=3`. That could create negative deltas when rollup computes current - previous if previous uses a higher offset timestamp.

erin: That matches. Short windows + offset rollback = earlier windows with counts lower than later windows -> negative deltas in token/sec rollups. Two fixes: (1) clamp negative deltas to 0 in aggregator to avoid spikes in dashboards, (2) run backfill replay for affected time range to recompute proper rollups. I'll prepare a tiny patch to clamp and a hotfix deploy.

devon: I'll run the backfill. Proposed command (run from data-tools container):
```
./tools/backfill --customer acme-inc --metric tokensec --from 2026-03-15T02:45:00Z --to 2026-03-15T04:00:00Z --strategy replay
```
Will run with `--dry-run` first to estimate row counts. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/data-tools/pull/482

maria: Customer is on a paid support plan, they're seeing billing dashboard anomalies too because some aggregation jobs feed the billing pipeline. We should prioritize.

jay: Rolling out clamp patch to staging now (small change in rollup service: `tokens = max(tokens, 0)`). I'll promote to prod after a quick smoke. Also created an alert rule: `streaming_rollup_negative_delta > 0` -> pager to oncall.

erin: After backfill and clamp deploy we should expect dashboards to normalize. Followups: add reconciliation that compares rollup sums vs raw kafka counts every 6h, add feature-flag for aggressive window shortening, and note in postmortem to avoid consumer resets without checkpoint persistence.

maria: Thanks team — I'll reply to customer with ETA: backfill + clamp deployed in next 30m, postmortem in 48h. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Note created: INC-2026-2453 linked to ticket #47891 for acme-inc streaming rollup negative deltas.

jay: Prod clamp deploy started at 2100012400, backfill job kicked at 2100012425 (dry-run). I'll post real numbers after dry-run completes.

devon: Dry-run estimate: 1.2M windows to recompute, expected to finish ~18m real time. If everything looks good we'll run live replay.

maria: Customer updated: they saw graphs normalize after the backfill (they confirmed). Closing customer-facing ticket after postmortem.

erin: Created follow-up tickets: `ENG-regen-rollup-clamp`, `DATA-rolling-backfill-automation`, `OPS-persistent-checkpoints`.

jay: Added playbook entry: if `rollup.window_ms` < 30000 then enable stronger checkpointing.

maria: Marking this thread done for support; will add final notes to internal ticket. :white_check_mark:
